title: metadax.technique/0.1
description: A teaching move captured as a content-free, language-independent unit so it can be reused across courses and languages. The move's subject nouns live only in rendered_examples; core carries no subject nouns. Keyed for retrieval by stuck_signature (a canonical learner-confusion category), not by content and not by language. This is the X01 reuse primitive and the fix proposed for bottleneck B18.

stuck_signature.description: The canonical learner-confusion category this move addresses. This is the retrieval key: a move is offered when a new learner's confusion matches this signature, regardless of subject or language.

stuck_detail.description: Optional free-text refinement of the signature for human curators. Not a retrieval key; must still contain no subject nouns if the move is to transfer.

chain_position.description: Who/what authored this move. Distinguishes a human-tutor move (tutor) from a model-played hint (model) so the two are not structurally identical (B18).

core.description: The language-neutral, subject-noun-free statement of the move: its intent, the trigger condition, the abstract shape, and guards against over-triggering.

rendered_examples.description: One or more concrete renderings of the move in specific languages/subjects. All subject nouns and scenario detail live here, never in core.

techniqueId.description: Opaque id: 't_' + 26 base32 (Crockford, no i/l/o/u), matching the v0.3 node id convention. Display name lives in slug.

stuckSignature.description: Canonical vocabulary of language- and subject-independent learner-confusion categories. Deliberately small and selective (guards against the over-triggering dead end): a move is retrieved only when its exact signature recurs. Extend by proposal, not ad hoc.

chainRole.description: tutor = a human teaching move; model = a model-played hint; author = course author; learner = learner-originated; curator = steward edit.

intent.description: What the move is for, stated with no subject nouns. E.g. 'make the learner assign each opposed quantity to the distinct owner it belongs to, so they stop treating two owners as one'.

trigger.description: The content-free condition under which to deploy the move — the shape of the learner's error. Should restate the stuck_signature concretely enough to be selective.

shape.description: The abstract form of the move itself, no subject nouns: the diagnostic question, framing, or analogy pattern the tutor performs.

guards.description: When NOT to use this move — selectivity conditions that prevent over-triggering.

lang.description: BCP-47 language tag of this rendering, e.g. 'en', 'id', or 'id-x-jv' for Indonesian code-switching into Javanese.

subject.description: The subject/domain this rendering was spoken in (nouns allowed here only).

example.description: The move as actually uttered to a learner in this language and subject.

back_translation.description: Optional English gloss, for curators judging core fidelity after translation.

minted_from.description: True if this is the rendering the technique was first minted from (the origin utterance).

status.description: Review lifecycle (ties to B21). Only accepted techniques propagate cross-fork by default.

reused_in.description: Languages (and optionally cohorts) this technique has been successfully applied in after minting.
